## Project thoughts
My research question is how do age and wealth impact a person's participation in election opinion polls? My hypothesis is that older and wealthier people participate at a higher rate in election opinion polls than younger and poorer people. I hypothesize this because older and wealthier people generally have more time to participate in these and may have more interest. Someone who is retired and is financially secure can spend their time doing something like an election opinion poll. However, a younger people who has to work a regular job may not have this time in their day, and they might also have less interest than a wealthier person who's wealth may be more directly impacted by the policies implemented after an election. My explanatory variables are age and wealth and these are measured by a person's age and by their net worth. The outcome variable is the rate of participation of different groups of people in election opinion polls. This can be measured by seeing what proportion of people who participate are above or below a certain age or amount of wealth. Something that would support my hypothesis would be seeing groups of people who are older and wealthier participating more in these polls than people who are younger and have less wealth. However, if I see that younger people with less wealth are participating more than I will see that my hypothesis is false.
